In the 1880s, Louis Pasteur developed vaccines for cholera and rabies. These were the first examples of killed vaccines, which use inactivated pathogens to stimulate an immune response. This paved the way for the development of inactivated vaccines, which use dead pathogens.

Shortly after, Albert Sabin developed an oral polio vaccine (OPV) in 1961, which used a live-attenuated poliovirus.

In the late 20th and early 21st centuries, several new vaccines were developed. The COVID-19 vaccines, developed at an unprecedented speed, were the first to use messenger RNA (mRNA) technology. They instruct the body to produce a harmless piece of the virus that triggers the immune system to produce antibodies.

Each of these vaccines has its own unique history and development process, but all have contributed to the control or eradication of certain diseases. The history of vaccine development is a testament to the power of science and the potential to improve global health.
